analysis:
The supplied units are head-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md, lines 1-797. The file_changes ranges show the actual changes are at head lines 1493-1505 and 1553-1586, which are outside the supplied excerpts. Only the patch excerpt shows them, and that excerpt is truncated. The Nemotron Super and GLM5Next documentation I could examine is unchanged context. It describes admission and memory ledgers, text-only prefix reuse partitioned by authenticated cache scope, and media reservations. I found nothing in it that changes a control or contradicts T-041, TB-007 or TB-002.

The visible patch is documentation only: the Qwen think-content seed with the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED=0 switch, and a section on streamed auto tool calls via ToolCallProcessor streaming options. Both describe code behavior changes outside this documentation file. Streamed tool-call deltas emit the name and then argument fragments before the call is fully validated. That could weaken the 'withheld until validated' behavior that the Nemotron text describes (lines 46-48). The Nemotron path is stated to use its own output parser, so it is likely unaffected. The tool-call streaming section is truncated in the excerpt, so I cannot confirm whether validation or tool-choice enforcement is preserved for streamed auto calls, or whether tool-call arguments could expose data beyond what the consumer already receives. The source code for ToolCallProcessor, ToolStreamPreparation and the Qwen seed was not supplied.

No security regression is demonstrated by the supplied evidence. A reviewer should check the corresponding Swift changes for partial-argument leakage on encryption or validation failure (T-008) and for tool-choice enforcement.
